name: Somali nationalism
summary: Somali nationalism holds that the Somali people, united by language, culture, ethnicity and overwhelmingly Islam, form one nation that should live in one state. Its central programme is Pan-Somalism or Greater Somalia, the union of the former British and Italian Somalilands with Somali-inhabited Ogaden, the Northern Frontier District and Djibouti. It rejects colonial borders and clan divisions and has no distinctive economic doctrine.
scope: The mainstream pan-Somali nationalism of the Somali Youth League and the 1960 Somali Republic, which pledged to pursue union by legal and peaceful means, together with the Barre-era turn to arms in the 1977 Ogaden War. Barre's Marxist-Leninist economics, post-1991 clan federalism and Somaliland separatism, and Al-Shabaab's Islamist use of the idea are excluded; economic and many social questions are therefore low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nothing in the nationalist programme addresses health care; a state that takes responsibility for its people's welfare, as Barre's republic claimed to, would lean toward it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Somali nationalism is a movement about nationhood and territory and has no wage policy, and the sources show adherents across economic camps.

public-ownership.rationale: Barre's nationalist regime nationalised major sectors after 1970, but the earlier SYL republic did not, so adherents split on state ownership.

strong-leader.rationale: The SYL competed in elections while Barre ruled as a strong leader; adherents have supported both, so the strand is split.

state-harmful.rationale: Somali nationalism seeks a unified Somali state and views statehood as the vehicle of the nation, so it rejects anarchism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Islam is the state religion under the 1960 constitution and Somali nationalism does not depart from it, so adherents oppose recognising same-sex marriage.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Somali nationalism concerns correcting colonial partition of Somalis, not racial injustice in the American sense, so the statement does not map onto it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Somali nationalism article treats shared language, culture and poetry as the basis of the nation, and the SYL worked to standardise the language and promote Somali interests.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The SYL appealed to the UN for trusteeship, but Somalia later defied it over borders; adherents have taken both stances.

nation-first.rationale: Pan-Somali nationalism puts the interests of the Somali nation, including claims on neighbours' land, ahead of existing international arrangements.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Barre justified the Ogaden invasion as liberating Somalis, but the doctrine of humanitarian intervention itself is not part of the ideology.

open-borders.rationale: Somali nationalists reject existing colonial borders for Somali lands but do not seek open borders generally; they want those borders redrawn to fit one nation.

revolution-justified.rationale: The SYL took a temperate course and the constitution stresses legal and peaceful means, yet Barre took power by coup and the WSLF waged guerrilla war; adherents are split.

central-planning.rationale: Barre's state adopted planning in the 1970s but the SYL-era republic did not, and the nationalist core is silent on economic systems.

socialized-markets.rationale: Socialism was the official language only under Barre; the earlier nationalist movement had no such programme.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The sources show no nationalist position on trade protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Barre's regime directed investment under a socialist plan, but the nationalist core does not require it, so adherents differ.

one-party-rule.rationale: The SYL contested elections and the 1960 constitution set up a multiparty republic; Barre's single-party rule after 1969 was imposed by coup rather than being the nationalist norm.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Somali nationalists refused to accept loss of the Ogaden, Haud and NFD; Barre suspended the Kenya claim only in 1981 and the Ethiopia border claim was never conceded in principle.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Barre's Somalia was a Soviet client until 1977 and then fell out with Moscow over Ethiopia, but the nationalist ideology has no analysis of Soviet economics.

collective-defense.rationale: Somalia sought allies, first the USSR then the US, but nationalists have no doctrine on collective-defence pacts.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Somali nationalists hold that Ethiopian and Kenyan rule over Somali lands lacks the consent of Somalis, who regarded the Ogaden as colonised.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Somali nationalism favours one unified Somalia, but the sources note Somaliland and Puntland's autonomy drives without recording a nationalist doctrine of force.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sovereignty belongs to the people under the constitution and the state is Islamic, which leaves no place for a divine-descent ruler.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The 1960 constitution gave the people sovereignty and equal rights before law, so a ruler above the law contradicts the nationalist republic; Barre's practice aside.

leader-cult.rationale: Barre built a personality cult while the SYL era did not, so adherents are split.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not a defining issue for the nationalist movement.

refugee-return.rationale: After the Ogaden War roughly 800,000 Ethiopian Somali refugees fled to Somalia, and nationalists framed Ogaden Somalis as part of the nation, so supporting their return to their homeland follows.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Somalism is exactly the claim to Somali-inhabited Ogaden, NFD, Djibouti and Haud because Somalis live there.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Somali nationalism seeks union of Somalis and the constitution speaks of solidarity among African and Islamic peoples, but a wider union of language-family kin is not the programme.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not the nationalist demand, which is territorial unification rather than autonomy within existing states.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Somali nationalists chose territorial union over fighting for minority rights inside Ethiopia and Kenya, though the WSLF mixed both aims.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Barre's rhetoric used Marxist terms but the nationalist core attributes change to national struggle rather than material conditions.

no-bailouts.rationale: The sources record no nationalist view on rescuing failing banks or firms, a question that arises in mature financial systems Somalia lacked.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The WSLF and Barre's army pursued armed struggle but there is no foco doctrine in the ideology.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalist writers trace the nation back through the Adal and Ajuran sultanates and the Darawiish, so teaching the nation's own history is a core cultural aim.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Somali nationalism arose in opposition to colonial rule and the SYL rejected the return of Italian rule, so tutelage by advanced societies is rejected.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Somali nationalists opposed colonial powers, but this concerns influence in former colonies; the statement is about the country's own former empire, which Somalia lacked, so low and mildly negative.

delink-world-market.rationale: Barre's socialism favoured self-reliance in rhetoric yet relied on aid, and the nationalist core is silent.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist idea absent from the nationalist core.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The constitution guarantees equal rights regardless of race, origin, language or religion, which cuts against a right to discriminate.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Pan-Somalism rejects the colonial partition of Somali lands among Britain, Italy, France and Ethiopia and the borders that resulted, calling the Ethiopia border artificial.

elective-rulers.rationale: The 1960 constitution made sovereignty belong to the people and the SYL contested elections.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Somali opposition movements resisted Barre, but nationalism has no doctrine on resisting rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1960 constitution created a parliamentary republic, but no doctrine of parliamentary supremacy is attributed to nationalists.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duties of the wealthy toward the poor do not appear in the nationalist sources; Islamic charity exists but is not tied to the ideology.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Somali nationalism is a mobilising political movement; the SYL and the Darawiish demanded active participation.

party-own-road.rationale: Barre argued at Aden that a true socialist view should support Somali self-determination, but the statement is about communist parties, not nationalism.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pan-Somalism demands recovery of Somali lands held by Ethiopia, Kenya and France, and Somalia fought the 1977 Ogaden War to take back the Ogaden.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The SYL opposed officials of the fascist-era Italian administration, but anti-fascism is not a founding value of Somali nationalism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparing fascism and communism is not a nationalist topic, and Somalia dealt with both Italian fascist rule and Soviet patrons without a recorded verdict.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Somali nationalists adopted a Western-style parliamentary constitution in 1960, but the ideology itself takes no stance.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Barre's army seized power in 1969, while the SYL's civilian republic put the army under government, so adherents are split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic labour is a feminist economic demand absent from the Somali nationalist programme.

single-official-language.rationale: The SYL pushed to standardise Somali as the national language and also wanted Arabic as an official language, so a single common language is promoted but not exclusively.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Restricting foreign land ownership might fit a nation-first outlook, but the sources record no rule or demand on it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is an American legal concept that does not map onto Somali nationalism, whose nation is one ethnic group.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Critiques of consumer culture do not appear in the nationalist sources, which are concerned with unification rather than lifestyle.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Somalia organised and armed the Western Somali Liberation Front in 1975 and supported insurgents against Kenya, so adherents accepted arming insurgents against neighbours' governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not a nationalist doctrine; Somalia resented Soviet-led intervention for Ethiopia in 1977.

non-intervention.rationale: Somalia intervened in Ogaden and supported insurgents in Kenya, and nationalists reject Ethiopian rule over Somalis as a matter of Somali concern rather than internal affairs.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The sources show no conspiracy theory about a minority in Somali nationalism; its grievance is with colonial powers and neighbouring states.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: With Islam the state religion and the constitution resting on Islamic doctrine, abolishing legal marriage is rejected.

local-production.rationale: Economic localism is not a nationalist theme in the sources; Somali pastoralism is central but is not framed as a policy of local production.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Somalia invoked self-determination in international bodies while rejecting borders set by treaties, so there is no fixed doctrine.

religious-nation.rationale: Somali nationalism defines the nation by ethnicity, language and culture, not religion, even though almost all Somalis are Muslim.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Somalia broke with the USSR and ended Soviet naval access when Moscow backed Ethiopia, and the SYL rejected foreign tutelage.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism became a live issue after 1991 but the nationalist core has no recorded view on regional revenue.

defeat-communism.rationale: Barre first allied with the USSR, then turned to the US, so anticommunism was not a doctrine of the ideology.

religion-illusion.rationale: The nationalist state is constitutionally Islamic and the Darawiish movement was a religious resistance, so calling religion an illusion contradicts the ideology.

treaties-binding.rationale: Somali nationalists treat colonial-era treaties handing Somali lands to Ethiopia and Britain as invalid, so they do not accept all state-nation treaties as binding.

majority-settlement.rationale: Somali nationalism treats Somali-inhabited regions as already Somali, and the sources record no policy of settling the majority in minority areas.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Barre's socialism and the earlier non-socialist republic show no consistent third-way position.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Nationalists trace Somali presence to medieval sultanates and claim lands on that ground and on current habitation, though the main argument is ethnic settlement.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Under an Islamic-state constitution with Islamic doctrine as a source of law, criminalisation is the expected position, though the sources read do not address it directly.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The SYL competed in a multiparty system; Barre's ban on parties after 1969 is a split from that tradition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The constitution makes Islam the religion of the state and forbids propagating other religions, which goes with punishing public blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Somali nationalism arose against colonial rule and the SYL opposed return of Italian administration, so colonies governed for the metropole are rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The Darawiish under Muhammad Abdullah Hassan fought colonial invaders in the name of Islam and are cited as precursors of the nationalism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Darawiish took religious grounds against colonial powers, but modern Somali nationalism does not treat secular rulers as illegitimate on religious grounds.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Islam is the state religion and nationalism does not depart from it, so legal recognition of gender identity is rejected.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Somali nationalism does not pronounce on the left-right axis; adherents ran both a liberal-democratic republic and a socialist regime.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The constitution gives sovereignty to the people while making Islamic doctrine the main source of law, so authority is popular in form with religious limits.

social-market-economy.rationale: The nationalist sources give no view on mixing markets with social protection, and adherents ran very different economic systems.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Ogaden War and the nationalist programme required a strong army, and abolishing it is not conceivable for adherents.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Somalia moved from the Soviet bloc to the US, and the SYL era courted both East and West, so no neutrality doctrine.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The constitutional republic vested sovereignty in the people and the SYL was a mass party, so hereditary succession does not fit Somali nationalism.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1960 constitution rests on equal rights regardless of status, and the SYL was a mass party, so limiting the vote by property is rejected.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Somali Republic was a republic with sovereignty in the people, and the nationalist tradition has no monarchist strand, so a hereditary head of state is not endorsed.

democracy-best.rationale: The SYL competed in elections and the 1960 constitution created a democratic republic, but Barre's nationalist regime was authoritarian, so adherents are split.

right-to-secede.rationale: The nationalist aim is union, and Somaliland and Puntland autonomy drives run against it, yet Ogaden Somalis' claim to leave Ethiopia is supported, so adherents split by case.

natural-rulers.rationale: The SYL banned clannishness and sought national unity beyond lineage, and the constitution gave equal rights regardless of birth.

political-violence-never.rationale: Somalia armed the WSLF and fought the Ogaden War, and the Darawiish fought colonial rule, so adherents do not renounce political violence.

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 1 of the 1960 constitution makes Islam the religion of the State, which a committed adherent would not trade for strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The 1960 constitution names Islamic doctrine as the main source of state laws, though nationalism is defined by ethnicity rather than religion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Nationalists seek a strong Somali state and army to defend and unify the nation, so private defence is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Somalia built a large army with Soviet aid to challenge Ethiopia in the Ogaden and lost a third of its regular army in the war, showing priority on military strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Somali nationalism article defines the nation by shared ethnicity, language and culture and calls for uniting all Somalis in one state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Somali nationalism treats the nation as unified across class and clan, and holds national and colonial struggle rather than class conflict to drive history.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not a nationalist theme, though the nation's claim to its homeland is related.

civilizational-union.rationale: The 1960 constitution commits the republic to solidarity with African and Islamic peoples, but union of Somalis, not of civilizations, is the programme.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The constitution lists both rights and duties and the sources do not rank them.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nationalists invoke past sultanates and the Darawiish as heritage, but the aim is unification in a modern state, not restoring an old order.

direct-action.rationale: The SYL used elections while the Darawiish and WSLF used armed struggle, so no common stance.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Somali nationalism aims at a modern unified state; a return to foraging is outside the ideology.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolishing the division of labour is a radical Marxist or utopian idea not found in the nationalist sources.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Barre's socialist language touched this but the nationalist core does not advance it.

production-for-use.rationale: Barre-era socialism used such language, but the nationalist core is silent.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Barre's socialism borrowed Marxist forms but Somali nationalism is built on a multi-class national unity.

collective-farming.rationale: Barre-era policy included cooperatives, but it is not a nationalist doctrine.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Barre's rhetoric about imperialism aside, the nationalist core has no such thesis.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nationalism treats the Somali nation as a rights-bearing community with claims to self-determination, so rights are not only individual.

conscription.rationale: Somalia raised a large army for the Ogaden War and the nationalist state required national service, so conscription is accepted.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The constitution makes sovereignty popular and the SYL contested elections, so voting counts for more than exit.

organic-representation.rationale: Clan structures matter in Somali society, but the SYL's anti-clan policy opposed clan-based representation, so the nationalist core is against.

total-state.rationale: Barre's state aimed at wide control, but the earlier nationalist republic was liberal in form, so the stance is split with a lean against.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not clearly a theme in the sources read.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pan-Somalism seeks to bring Somali-inhabited territory under one state, but this is framed as reunification of Somalis rather than expansion for its own sake.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The constitution rests on popular sovereignty and the SYL rejected clan loyalty politics.

bound-labor.rationale: Equal rights under the 1960 constitution and the nationalist emphasis on freedom from colonial rule contradict bonded labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A postmodern or critical-theory claim not found in the nationalist sources.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources read do not address this; Somalia is a member of the Arab League and generally hostile to Israel, but this is not part of the ideology itself.

revive-national-language.rationale: Somali was a living language and the SYL standardised its script, so the statement about reviving a disused language does not apply.

national-self-determination.rationale: Pan-Somalism demands that Somalis, as one nation, govern themselves in a single state, and Barre argued at Aden that socialism should support Somali self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Somalia invaded the Ogaden in 1977 without UN or great-power approval, so adherents have accepted force without UN backing.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Islam is the state religion of the republic, so faith is not subordinated to reason.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalists stress national unity across social divisions rather than class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nationalists value cultural heritage such as poetry and the Darawiish legacy as foundations of the nation.

dominated-front.rationale: The constitution commits to solidarity with African and Islamic peoples, and Somalia fought alongside Cold War patrons, but a front against Western powers is not an explicit aim.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: An Islamic-state republic with Islamic doctrine as source of law leans toward distinct roles, though equal rights before law are also stated.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The constitution guarantees equal rights regardless of race, and nationalism's quarrel is with colonial discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist language appeared under Barre but is not part of the nationalist core.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigrant assimilation is not a nationalist theme, since Somali nationalism is concerned with Somalis across borders rather than with newcomers.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of this kind is not part of the sources.

national-mission.rationale: The sources describe an aim of uniting Somalis rather than a mission to spread a form of government to others.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Barre and later Somali critics made charges of corruption, but it is not a defining claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not Somali nationalist doctrine, and Islamic norms and equal rights provisions oppose it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Barre-era abuses were later a major issue, but accountability is not a nationalist position.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Nationalists want an active state to unify the nation and defend it.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Somali identity is defined by language and culture, not purity of descent, so discouraging mixing is not a nationalist position.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution gives citizens equal rights and duties before the law regardless of race, origin, language, religion or sex.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Barre's state built socialism nationally; the question does not arise in the nationalist core.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The constitution grants equality before the law but also names Islamic doctrine as a main source, and Somalia has no major non-Muslim community.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article 29 of the 1960 constitution bans spreading any religion other than Islam.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Somali pastoralists depend on livestock and Islam is the state religion, so banning cattle slaughter is out of the question.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: With Islam the religion of the state, state schools giving religious instruction is expected.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Barre-era rhetoric about threats aside, it is a Marxist-Leninist thesis not held by the nationalist core.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The constitution places sovereignty in the people.

population-transfer.rationale: Nationalists took in Ogaden refugees and sought to unify Somali lands rather than expel minorities, and the sources record no such doctrine.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The 1960 constitution commits to legal and peaceful means of union, but Barre's invasion of the Ogaden shows adherents did not hold force wrong in principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The sources do not present a Social Darwinist theory of struggle between peoples as the engine of progress, even though nationalists fought wars.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1960 constitution created a republic with separate branches; nationalism itself has no doctrine on it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Barre's party was modelled on Leninist lines but the nationalist core relies on mass national unity, not a vanguard.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy question unrelated to Somali nationalism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Somali nationalists claim the nation is ethnically homogeneous and unify on that basis, but they do not state that diversity itself weakens cohesion.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Barre's regime suspended the constitution after 1969, but nationalism as such has no doctrine.

party-controls-media.rationale: The SYL era had open elections and the constitution protects expression, while Barre's regime controlled media, so the nationalist core leans against.

party-commands-army.rationale: The 1960 constitution kept the army under the state, while Barre's later single-party system moved otherwise, so the core leans against.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Capping legislators' pay is a socialist demand not found in the nationalist sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The SYL was a mass party but no doctrine on party discipline is documented.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The constitution speaks of solidarity with African and Islamic peoples, yet nationalists insist on sovereignty for the Somali nation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 1960 constitution created a parliamentary republic with a president, but nationalism has no doctrine on who commands the forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Islam has no bishops, so the statement does not apply to the Somali nationalist setting.

clerical-rule.rationale: Islam is the state religion and a source of law, but the constitution places sovereignty in the people rather than in religious scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalists backed their own state's war in the Ogaden and the Darawiish fought colonial armies, so working for the government's defeat is rejected.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Barre ruled for 22 years without competitive elections, while the republic had elected presidents; no settled stance.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Somalia sought alliances with the USSR and then the US to pursue its claims, so ending alliances is not nationalist policy.

people-in-arms.rationale: Pastoral society was widely armed and the WSLF was a popular force, but Somalia also built a professional army, so adherents are split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Somalism is exactly this claim: Somali lands divided among Britain, Italy, France and Ethiopia are to be united in one state, and the 1960 constitution commits the republic to promote the union of Somali territories.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The constitution makes Islam the state religion and restricts other religions, so exemptions for minorities are not a theme.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Barre's socialist turn linked independence to economic change, but the earlier nationalist movement did not.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Barre's regime restricted freedom under a development banner, but the SYL era did not, so adherents split.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Under the 1960 constitution the president was chosen by the assembly, but no nationalist doctrine is recorded.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept absent from the nationalist sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The constitution sets a rule-of-law republic, but no nationalist doctrine on this is documented.

racial-franchise.rationale: The constitution gives equal rights regardless of race, origin, language or religion, and the 1960 republic was a democratic one.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: No such tradition is documented in Somali nationalism.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The constitution names Islamic doctrine as a source of law without a reform programme.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Islam is the state religion and the constitution forbids propagating other religions, so state atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nationalism wants a strong unified state that holds the means of order.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Somali nationalism treats Somalia as one nation and the SYL opposed clannishness, yet clan balance in government became common practice; split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Islamic charity is a value, but no nationalist position on state aid is documented.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The constitution gives equal rights to men and women before the law but also rests on Islamic doctrine, so the stance is not settled.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Barre later organised youth groups, but this is not found in the SYL-era nationalist core.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Somalia hosted Soviet naval facilities and later US access, and expelled the Soviets only after the 1977 break, so no stable doctrine.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nationalists fought defensive and offensive wars, and the Darawiish resisted colonialism by force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Somali nationalism article traces the nation from the medieval Adal and Ajuran sultanates through the Darawiish to the modern movement.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Darawiish treated resistance as religious struggle, but modern nationalism does not frame politics as good against evil in general.

culture-before-state.rationale: Nationalists such as the SYL pursued political unification and independence, with culture as a means rather than a prior step.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-Somalism seeks to merge Somali-inhabited Ogaden, NFD and Djibouti with the Somali Republic as one territorial unit.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1960 constitution had a unicameral assembly, but no nationalist doctrine on chambers is documented.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Nationalism favours a unified state over loose confederation, though federalism is debated after 1991.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Life-extension research is a modern issue outside Somali nationalist writing.

person-over-state.rationale: The constitution protects personal integrity and rights, yet nationalism puts the nation first; split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Nationalism prefers a unified state and regions as parts of it, but federalism after 1991 complicates this.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Somali nationalism organises around ethnic-national interests, but the statement concerns race as a political category, which the sources do not use.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Somali heritage is nationalist, but framing it as race is not how the sources describe it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Barre's invasion of the Ogaden was justified as liberation rather than defence, and the claims on neighbours' land mean adherents do not limit force to defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Somali nationalism article bases the nation on shared language, culture and ethnicity across states, and the SYL promoted a standard Somali script.

communal-electorates.rationale: The SYL banned clannishness and built a national party, so separate communal electorates oppose its approach.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Barre's state sought a monopoly while clan militias and the WSLF held arms; split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nationalist armies fought the Ogaden War and Darawiish fought colonial rule, so refusal is contrary to the ideology.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The nationalist aim is to take and extend a Somali state, and the republic was a constitutional one, so smashing the state is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The sources show no nationalist stance on communities choosing different economic systems.

sacred-nation.rationale: Nationalists revere the nation, and Darawiish tradition mixes religion with national resistance, but the sources do not call it sacred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Ogaden Somalis saw Ethiopian rule as colonial subjugation, which is the claim that one state's centre exploits its periphery as a colony.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Islam is the state religion and the constitution forbids propagation of others, so a claim that all religions share one truth is not nationalist.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The constitution gives equal rights, but Islamic inheritance rules differ for women, so the position is not settled.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Somali nationalism treats Somali as one language across all regions and clans, and the SYL built a standard script for it.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Clan elders play a role in Somali politics but the SYL opposed clannishness, so the nationalist core is split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The sources give no definition of democracy; the SYL contested elections but the nationalist core does not define the term.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1960 constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of sex, and women voted in the republic.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Islam is the state religion of the nationalist republic, so adherents reject the claim.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Nationalists claimed lands through force and rejected outside rulings on borders, so submitting leaders to international tribunals is not a nationalist position.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Barre's state had planned elements, but the nationalist core does not defend them.

national-church-status.rationale: Islam is the religion of the state with a special status under the 1960 constitution, which bars propagating other religions.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Nationalists want Somali territories united, and Somaliland and Puntland autonomy move is against the unitary aim.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Pan-Somalism rejects the colonial borders that divide Somali lands, and Al-Shabaab calls the Ethiopia border artificial.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The nationalist sources link the Somali nation to its inhabited lands from the medieval sultanates onward, and defending them was the motive for Ogaden war.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The constitution guarantees the right to life and personal integrity.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Somalia supported Somalis in Ogaden and the NFD, organising the WSLF and aiding insurgents in Kenya, as the core of its policy.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The SYL was a party and the republic multiparty; Barre later suppressed parties, so the core leans against bypassing them.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Somali Muslims are mostly Sunni, so denominational politics is not a live issue for nationalism.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The programme is about one nation in one state, and its sources do not link patriotism to working-class politics.

missingStatements.text: Political loyalty to one's clan should be set aside in favour of loyalty to the nation.
missingStatements.rationale: The Somali Youth League banned clannishness and its founders declined to disclose their clans to promote national unity.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to clan-based societies; existing statements on ethnic and national identity place the ideology.

missingStatements.text: Islam should be the official religion of the state.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 1 of the 1960 constitution declares that Islam shall be the religion of the State.

notes: Barre's regime combined Greater Somalia with Marxist-Leninist rhetoric and one-party rule, whereas the SYL republic was multiparty and committed to peaceful means; answers marked low or 0 on those points reflect that split. Several answers on family law and sexuality are inferred from the constitution's Islamic basis rather than from nationalist texts.
